meta.title: The room | {{brand.name}} for hosts
meta.description: A first hello with a mission at check-in, groups, tables, teams and rotations built for each format, and Help me say hi for introductions you make. No app for guests, and joining in is always optional.
meta.socialDescription: Nobody comes to stand by the wall. The room on {{brand.name}}.

sections.title: Nobody comes to stand by the wall.
sections.lead: Most event tools stop at the ticket. {{brand.name}} is built for what people actually came for: meeting people. A first hello with a mission, groups that mix, introductions you make when a guest asks, and a console that shows you who hasn’t been put in a group.

sections.title: The first ten minutes decide the whole night.
sections.lead: People leave events saying “it was fine” when they spoke to no one new. Each of these is a moment {{brand.name}} is built to fix.

items.title: Arriving alone is the hardest part
items.body: Walking into a room of strangers, looking for a face.
items.fix: First Hello gives a guest someone to find the moment they check in.

items.title: Small talk needs a reason
items.body: “So, what do you do?” for the fifth time.
items.fix: A mission gives two people something to do together, not just something to say.

items.title: Nobody wants to be the one who asks
items.body: Someone they’d like to talk to is across the room.
items.fix: Help me say hi lets them ask you quietly, and you make the introduction.

sections.title: A first hello, with a mission.
sections.lead: When guests check in, {{brand.name}} gives each one a person or a small group to find, and something to do together: find out where they ran their first 5K, agree on the best vada pav nearby, pick a team name. It’s a reason to talk that isn’t small talk.

sections.title: Every format, set up for people to meet.
sections.lead: A pace group, a long table and a quiz team are different rooms. {{brand.name}} builds each one for its format, and you can move anyone before or during the night.

items.label: Run clubs
items.title: Sunday Social Run
items.subtitle: Driftwood Bay Runners · Sandbar Promenade, Bandra
items.body: People are moving, so phones stay in pockets. {{brand.name}} does its work before the start and after the finish.

list.title: Pace groups, set before Sunday
list.body: Runners give their pace before the run. {{brand.name}} builds pods at a similar pace, and you can move anyone before the run.

list.title: Check in, then pocket the phone
list.body: Runners check in at the meeting point and see their pod once. While the run is on, {{brand.name}} sends them nothing.

list.title: A first hello at the start line
list.body: Each pod gets one question to answer together before they set off, so the first kilometre already has a conversation in it.

list.title: Nobody left on the road
list.body: At the finish, you or your sweep mark each runner back. Anyone not marked stays on your list until you close the run.

list.title: The next run, already easier
list.body: Runners get a feedback prompt after the finish, and your report shows who came for the first time and who came back.

items.label: Dinners
items.title: Long Table Supper
items.subtitle: Saffron Table · Khar West
items.body: Phones are within reach all evening, and the point is to leave them there. {{brand.name}} sets the table, then gets out of the way.

list.title: Tables planned from who’s coming
list.body: {{brand.name}} suggests tables from your guest list, keeping friends who booked together side by side, and you adjust with a tap.

list.title: One look at the phone, then dinner
list.body: Guests check in and see their seat once. After that, nothing at dinner needs a phone.

list.title: The whole room at a glance
list.body: The seating map shows who’s where. Seat a late arrival or move someone with a tap, and table sizes and anyone you’ve kept apart still hold.

list.title: A new seat for dessert
list.body: Between courses, {{brand.name}} can re-seat the room so everyone meets a few more people. Conversation cards are there if you want them.

list.title: Hear how it went
list.body: Guests get a feedback prompt, and can say privately who they talked to. You see the totals, never who named whom.

items.label: Games and quizzes
items.title: Tuesday Trivia Night
items.subtitle: Lantern Lane Social · Harbour Room, Bandra West
items.body: Heads are down during rounds and up between them. {{brand.name}} only speaks in the gaps, and keeps the scores.

list.title: Fair teams before the first question
list.body: {{brand.name}} builds teams of five from who’s coming: friends who booked together stay together, and people on their own are spread across teams.

list.title: A team for everyone at the door
list.body: Guests check in and see their team and table on their phone.

list.title: Mix the teams between rounds
list.body: If you want, people move to new tables between rounds so everyone meets someone new. Guests hear about it only at the change.

list.title: Scores in, standings hidden
list.body: You enter each round’s scores. The standings stay hidden until you reveal them, so the last round still matters.

list.title: The reveal
list.body: Start a countdown, and the final standings appear on every guest’s phone at once.

items.label: Pickleball
items.title: Pickleball Social
items.subtitle: Dink and Drink · Andheri West · 40 players, 3 courts
items.body: Forty players, three courts. Phones come out between games, and {{brand.name}} makes sure everyone gets their share of court time.

list.title: Levels in, courts planned
list.body: Players give their level before the session. {{brand.name}} plans the rounds on your courts so everyone gets about the same time on court.

list.title: Check in, then play
list.body: Players check in at the door. Anyone arriving late joins the next round.

list.title: A new partner every round
list.body: Between games, phones show the next court and partner. Nobody plays with the same partner twice until the rotation runs out.

list.title: Court time, counted
list.body: You see every player’s minutes on court and on the bench. Anyone sitting out is pointed to the common area to mix.

list.title: Standings, when you’re ready
list.body: Record each round’s results, and reveal the final standings at the end.

items.label: Pub crawls
items.title: Friday Bandra Pub Crawl
items.subtitle: Night Shift Socials · four stops in Bandra
items.body: The night moves, so the plan has to travel with it. Phones come out between stops, and {{brand.name}} keeps count of everyone along the way.

list.title: Plan the route
list.body: Set the stops, and give your helpers a lead or sweep role for the night.

list.title: A first hello at the first bar
list.body: Guests check in and get one icebreaker to do with someone in the group, so people are mixing before the first move.

list.title: Move between venues
list.body: When the group leaves a stop, your lead confirms who left and where you’re heading next.

list.title: Late arrivals find the group
list.body: Someone arriving late is pointed to the stop you’ve confirmed you’re at, not the first one.

list.title: The end-of-night sweep
list.body: At the last stop, mark everyone accounted for. Anyone not marked stays on your list before you close the night.

sections.title: Want to meet someone? Ask the host, quietly.
sections.lead: A guest can tell you privately that they’d like to meet someone: a person they noticed, or just “someone else who climbs”. The request shows on your live console with their note, and you decide whether to make the introduction. The other guest isn’t told unless you do.

sections.title: Joining in is always a choice.
sections.lead: Meeting people only works when everyone feels free to join in, or not. These rules hold in every format.

items.title: Joining in is optional
items.body: Guests can skip any mission, group activity or introduction.

items.title: Only what’s needed
items.body: Guests see their own group, table or team, never the full guest list.

items.title: Blocks are respected
items.body: Nobody is paired with someone they’ve blocked or reported.

items.title: Report anything, privately
items.body: A safety report goes to {{brand.name}}’s safety team, never to the other guest.

items.question: Do guests have to take part?
items.answer: No. Every mission, group activity and introduction can be skipped, and guests who skip still get the night they booked.

items.question: Who sees a Help me say hi request?
items.answer: Only you and your team. The other guest isn’t told unless you decide to make the introduction.

items.question: Does this work for my format?
items.answer: Runs, dinners, quizzes, racket sports and pub crawls have their own grouping. For anything else, pick an open format and choose the tools you want.

items.question: Do guests need the app?
items.answer: No. First Hello, groups and introductions work in the phone’s browser after a quick phone check.

items.answer: Yes. Start from the missions written for your format, edit them, or write your own for the night.
